subject: Extending map_data to include ZCTA (ZIP) map data

messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: Extending map_data to include ZCTA (ZIP) map data
parts:
I have written a package called choroplethr that facilitates creating choropleth maps in R.  At the core, the package uses ggplot2 to get state and county level maps as data.frames and then colors them in as described in Winston Chang's book "R Graphics Cookbook".

It also renders zip level data maps as scatterplots, getting the longitude and latitude coordinates from the package zipcode.  This is because map_data does not have a "zip" level map.  While I do not have extensive experience with maps, I do realize that there are a lot of problems with mapping zips.  

What I would like to do is render the same boundaries that the Census uses for their ZIP Code Tabulated Areas (ZCTAs).  Those boundaries are available as a shapefile here.  However, this file is huge (501MB zipped), and my first naive attempt to plot it took forever.  

My question is this: is there any way to convert this file into the same output that I would get with map_data?  Also, will the resulting data.frame be of a manageable size?

Thanks.

Ari

messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: Re: Extending map_data to include ZCTA (ZIP) map data
parts:
As a further point, I discovered this document on the ggplot2: plotting polygon shapefiles.  But when I get to this line:

  zcta.points = fortify(zcta, region="id")
RStudio just seems to hang.  (The actual line in the doc is utah.points because it's a Utah-related shapefile, but I am using the census' ZCTA shapefile, so I renamed the variables).  

I wasn't sure if it was just taking a long time due to the file size or was truly hanging, so I let it run overnight.  It didn't complete.
